title: Simulating Competition and Logistic Growth
beats: Unchecked exponential growth has no limits in reality; show the S-shaped curve we want.
Previous setup: stepwise sim and the expected-change equation delta = (R - D) N; plot it.
R > D case: straight line, positive slope, exponential growth; pointer to earlier video.
Work backward from the desired curve: levels off at 50, so delta must be zero at N = 50.
Make death more likely when crowded; add a term proportional to N.
Crowding coefficient as short name; 0.001 means each extra creature adds 0.1% death chance to all.
With looked-ahead value 0.001, delta is zero at 50 because death equals replication.
Terms carrying capacity and logistic growth curve given after the behaviour.
Check the delta curve region by region (exponential, plateau of growth rate, slowing, above capacity negative).
Run sim; roughly works; chance means look at many runs.
Add mutants: green slightly worse replication, orange lower death, sharing the total crowding term.
Predict; orange takes over; green beats blue by luck so the most likely outcome does not always happen.
Replication, mutation, competition are evolution's core; next, natural selection instead of artificial.

new_moves.name: work-backward-from-target-shape
new_moves.what: Draw the curve you want, derive what the equation must do at the key point, then choose the simplest term that does it

new_moves.name: looked-ahead-disclosure
new_moves.what: Admit the parameter was chosen so the answer comes out, rather than pretending it was discovered

new_moves.name: region-by-region-check
new_moves.what: Verify a derived formula by walking through each region of its graph and predicting the sim

theory: The video demonstrates invention-by-constraints: state the shape you want, find the condition that shape requires, pick the smallest term that satisfies it, then verify region by region. The learner is led to propose the term (proportional to N) instead of receiving it. It trades long examples for a compact, logically ordered derivation, so it relies on prior videos.
velocity: Orchestrator: add a work-backward playbook (target curve, key condition, simplest term, verify).
Scene builder: overlay desired curve vs formula-generated curve, and walk regions with a highlighting pointer.
Voice: disclose when a parameter was tuned.
Learner model: video assumes prerequisites; gate short derivation scenes on a prerequisite check or recap beat.
